skill.name: env-manager
skill.description: Manage environment variable documentation, validation patterns, and secret-handling guidance for applications.
skill.summary: Helps teams document, validate, and secure application environment variables.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged many examples related to .env files, credential names, URLs, Markdown backticks, and secret-management commands. Review found these are documentation examples for environment validation and defensive secret handling, with no prompt injection, hidden execution path, or data exfiltration intent in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Example placeholders resemble real credentials and inflate automated risk signals.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly invalid placeholders such as <AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID> and <STRIPE_SECRET_KEY> instead of realistic prefixes like AKIA or sk_test.

remediation.issue: Documentation asks users to inspect environment files, which can expose local secrets to an AI assistant if copied verbatim.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to redact secret values before sharing output and to report only variable names, presence, and validation errors by default.

remediation.issue: The cascading dotenv example uses NODE_ENV in a file path.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain NODE_ENV to a fixed allowlist before selecting environment-specific files.

static_findings.snippet: throw new Error('API_KEY environment variable is required');
- Never commit actual `.env` files with secrets

content.value_statement: Environment variables are easy to miss, misname, or expose during development. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code document variables, validate formats, and improve secret-handling practices.
actual_capabilities: Identifies environment variables referenced in application code.
Builds .env.example style templates with required and optional variables.
Suggests validation rules for URLs, numbers, booleans, and enumerated values.
Documents environment variables with descriptions, defaults, and security notes.
Recommends secret-management practices for development and production.
Highlights common configuration mistakes such as missing values and string boolean checks.
limitations: It does not rotate, revoke, or store secrets for you.
It may need project-specific context to identify every runtime variable.
It should not receive raw production secret values in prompts or shared files.
It provides examples, not a complete compliance review of secret storage.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Service
use_cases.description: Generate a clean environment variable template before a new application is shared with the team.

use_cases.title: Audit Deployment Configuration
use_cases.description: Check whether required variables are documented and validated before staging or production release.

use_cases.title: Improve Onboarding Docs
use_cases.description: Create readable setup instructions that explain each variable and safe local defaults.

prompt_templates.title: List Environment Variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use env-manager to list the environment variables used by this project. Group them by required and optional variables.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Example File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use env-manager to draft a .env.example template for this service. Use placeholders only and include short descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Configuration Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use env-manager to propose validation rules for each environment variable, including type, allowed values, defaults, and required status.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Secret Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use env-manager to review our environment configuration for secret-handling risks. Do not print secret values. Report only variable names, risk level, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Document the environment variables for a Node.js API.
output: A grouped list of required application, database, cache, and security variables.
A template with placeholder values and short comments.
Validation recommendations for ports, URLs, booleans, and log levels.

output_examples.input: Check whether our configuration is safe for production.
output: A finding that production secrets should be stored in a secrets manager.
A warning to avoid committing local .env files.
A checklist for required variables and environment-specific settings.

output_examples.input: Help onboard a new developer to local configuration.
output_examples.output: A concise setup guide that explains required variables, safe placeholder values, and validation steps.

best_practices: Share variable names and placeholders, not real secret values.
Validate required variables during application startup.
Keep committed templates separate from local or production secret files.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production secrets into prompts or generated documentation.
Do not rely on undocumented defaults for required deployment settings.
Do not commit .env files that contain credentials or private endpoints.

faq.question: Can this skill create a .env.example file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a template with placeholders, descriptions, required status, and safe example values.

faq.question: Does it read my real secrets?
faq.answer: It should not need real secret values. Provide variable names, code references, or redacted samples instead.

faq.question: Can it validate environment variable types?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest validation for URLs, ports, numbers, booleans, strings, and allowed choices.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a secret manager?
faq.answer: No. It documents and reviews configuration practices, but it does not store, rotate, or provision secrets.

faq.question: Can it help with production readiness?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review required variables, unsafe defaults, missing validation, and secret-management recommendations.
